badges.name: Camping
badges.summary: Plan, pack and cook for campouts, and camp at least 20 nights.

requirements.summary: Know how to stay safe while camping.

children.summary: Explain camping hazards and how to prevent and handle them.
Explain why weather matters and how to prepare for storms.
Show first aid for common camping injuries and illnesses.

requirements.summary: Learn and plan to follow Leave No Trace and the Outdoor Code.
Plan an overnight trek and find your way with a topo map.

children.summary: Use a compass.
Use a GPS receiver.
Use a smartphone GPS app.

requirements.summary: Help organize campouts.

children.summary: Make a duty roster for your patrol's overnight campout.
Help a patrol or Webelos unit get ready for a campout.

requirements.summary: Know how to dress and pack for a campout.

children.summary: List warm- and cold-weather clothing, and explain layering.
Discuss the right footwear for different weather.
Explain how to care for and store clothing, footwear and bedding.
List the Scout Basic Essentials and why each is needed.
Have your Scoutmaster inspect you and your pack.

requirements.summary: Learn about tents, water, packs and sleeping gear.

children.summary: Compare four kinds of tents, and pitch one with a partner.
Explain camp sanitation, and treat water two ways.
Explain how to choose a good tent site.
Compare internal- and external-frame packs.
Choose and care for a sleeping bag, and make a ground bed.

requirements.summary: Get ready for a patrol overnight campout.

children.summary: List the personal and patrol gear you'll need.
Pack your gear and your share of patrol gear properly.

requirements.summary: Plan and cook camp meals.

children.summary: Explain stove and fuel safety.
Propane or butane stoves.
Liquid-fuel stoves.
Storing extra fuel.
Compare kinds of lightweight stoves.
Plan a seven-meal camp menu and food list for your patrol.
Cook three planned meals at camp, one on a lightweight stove.

requirements.summary: Build your camping experience.

children.summary: Camp at least 20 nights at Scouting activities.
On your campouts, do two outdoor adventures.
Hike up a mountain, climbing at least 1,000 feet.
Backpack, snowshoe or cross-country ski at least 4 miles.
Bike at least 15 miles or four hours.
Take a nonmotorized water trip of 5 miles or four hours.
Plan and go on an overnight snow campout.
Rappel down a route of at least 30 feet.
On a campout, do an approved conservation project.

requirements.summary: Discuss what camping taught you and how Scout ideals apply.

badges.name: Citizenship in the Community
badges.summary: Learn how your local community works and volunteer to help it.

requirements.summary: Discuss what it takes to be a good citizen in your community.
Get to know your community and its government.

children.summary: Map local places and record how far they are from home.
Government buildings, such as city hall and the courthouse.
The nearest fire station, police station and hospital.
Parks, playgrounds, recreation areas and trails.
Historic or other interesting places.
Chart your local or state government's top offices.

requirements.summary: See local government at work.

children.summary: Attend a local government meeting in person.
Explain which side you favored on an issue debated there.

requirements.summary: Look into a local issue that matters to you.

children.summary: Find which branch of local government handles it.
Interview someone from that branch about it.
Share what you learned with your counselor.

requirements.summary: Watch and discuss a movie about someone improving their community.
List taxpayer-funded local services and why they matter.
Get to know a local charity and volunteer for it.

children.summary: Find three local charities outside Scouting that interest you.
Research one of them.
Volunteer at least eight hours for it, then discuss.

requirements.summary: Present your community's history, people, highlights and challenges.

badges.name: Citizenship in the Nation
badges.summary: Learn how the U.S. government works and how citizens take part.

requirements.summary: Explain what the Constitution is, what it does and why it matters.
List the Preamble's six purposes and how they affect you.
Explain the three branches of the federal government.

children.summary: What each branch does.
Why power is split among branches.
How the branches check and balance each other.
How citizens can take part in each branch.

requirements.summary: Explain why these founding documents and ideas matter.

children.summary: The Declaration of Independence.
The Bill of Rights and the 14th Amendment.
E Pluribus Unum, the traditional national motto.

requirements.summary: Follow the national news for five days and discuss one issue.
Study a speech that shaped the nation's history.

children.summary: Who gave it.
Its historical setting.
The national problems it addressed.
What it said.
Why it matters to the nation's history.
Pick a line that speaks to you and explain why.

requirements.summary: Visit or research places of national importance.

children.summary: Visit a National Historic Landmark or registered historic place.
Tour your state capitol or the U.S. Capitol.
Tour a federal facility.
Research a national monument and why it matters.

requirements.summary: Write to your member of Congress about a national issue.

badges.name: Citizenship in the World
badges.summary: Learn how nations govern, cooperate and relate to one another.

requirements.summary: Explain what being a citizen of the world means to you.
Explain how people become U.S. citizens, and compare rights across countries.
Look at how events and geography shape nations.

children.summary: Show how a current event affects a country's relationships.
Show how a country's land and climate shape its economy.

requirements.summary: Explore how nations work together.

children.summary: Explain how international law helps settle disputes.
Follow a world trade issue and why cooperation matters.
Describe the work of two international organizations.
The United Nations and UNICEF.
The International Court of Justice.
Interpol.
The World Organization of the Scout Movement.
The World Health Organization.
Amnesty International.
The Red Cross and Red Crescent.
CARE.
The European Union.

requirements.summary: Compare forms of government around the world.

children.summary: Contrast constitutional and non-constitutional governments.
Name five kinds of government in use today.
Find countries using each kind on a world map.

requirements.summary: Explain how countries represent themselves abroad.

children.summary: How nations are represented abroad and in world bodies.
Explain the roles of four U.S. diplomatic and trade offices.
What passports and visas are for.

requirements.summary: Do two activities and share what you learned.

children.summary: Research a world issue using State Department resources.
Find a foreign news story about a right people lack there.
Learn about another culture from a young person who lives there.
Join a world Scouting event, in person, by radio or online.
Attend an international festival or cultural event.

badges.name: Communication
badges.summary: Practice listening, speaking, writing and presenting to different audiences.

requirements.summary: Look at how you communicate.

children.summary: Log a day of your communication activities.
Keep a three-day journal of your listening.
Share stories in a small group and observe how each person communicates.
List ways to communicate and when each works poorly.

requirements.summary: Present yourself or an idea.

children.summary: Describe yourself creatively and present it to your counselor.
Make a sales pitch for something you believe in.

requirements.summary: Write a five-minute speech and give it to a group.
Interview someone and introduce them as a guest speaker.
Attend a public meeting and report every side fairly.
Plan and teach a skill, then check what was learned.
Share your writing with others.

children.summary: Write to a newspaper or magazine editor.
Build a webpage or blog with three entries.
Design a newsletter, brochure or flyer for a group.

requirements.summary: Plan and emcee a court of honor, campfire or interfaith service.
Explore careers in communication and study one closely.

badges.name: Cooking
badges.summary: Learn food safety and nutrition, and cook at home, in camp and on the trail.

requirements.summary: Know how to cook and handle food safely.

children.summary: Explain cooking hazards and how to prevent and handle them.
Show first aid for burns, cuts, choking and allergic reactions.
Explain safe food storage and how to avoid cross-contamination.
Discuss food allergies, intolerances and foodborne illness.
Explain food labels and how to spot common allergens.

requirements.summary: Learn the basics of good nutrition.

children.summary: Give examples, servings and serving sizes for each food group.
Explain why to limit oils and sugars.
Track your activity and calorie needs for five days.
Discuss your eating habits and how to eat healthier.
Explain food label terms and work out nutrition for two servings.

requirements.summary: Learn cooking basics.

children.summary: Discuss ten cooking methods, their equipment and heat control.
Compare cooking on a camp stove with a charcoal or wood fire.
Explain how to time a meal so everything is ready together.
Explain how taste, texture and smell affect what we eat.

requirements.summary: Cook at home.

children.summary: Plan three days of meals plus a dessert.
Find recipes, make a shopping list and cost each meal.
Review your plan and shopping list with your counselor.
Cook breakfast, lunch, dinner and dessert using five methods.
Time each meal, and have an adult confirm you cooked it.
Get feedback on each meal and discuss what you learned.

requirements.summary: Cook at camp.

children.summary: Plan four meals, a snack and a dessert for your patrol.
Find recipes, scale them, and budget the cost per person.
Review your menus and shopping list with your counselor.
Cook the four meals outdoors using the required methods.
Make the snack and dessert outdoors.
Get feedback on each meal and discuss what you learned.
Lead cleanup, and handle leftovers and waste properly.
Discuss how you followed Leave No Trace and the Outdoor Code.

requirements.summary: Cook on the trail.

children.summary: Plan a day of lightweight trail meals and a snack.
Make a shopping list and cost each meal.
Review your menu and repackaging plan with your counselor.
Cook two meals and a snack on a hike or backpacking trip.
Get feedback on each meal and discuss what you learned.
Explain sharing the load, cleanup and protecting food from animals.

requirements.summary: Look at cooking in your future.

children.summary: Explore careers in cooking and study one closely.
Explore how cooking could become a hobby or healthy habit.

badges.name: Environmental Science
badges.summary: Study ecosystems, pollution and conservation, and how people affect nature.

requirements.summary: Explain environmental science in your own words and how it helps.
Study an ecosystem.

children.summary: Observe an approved area's ecosystem over two days.
Note its parts, how they interact, and how people affect it.

requirements.summary: Explore air pollution.

children.summary: Learn about particulate matter and test for it.
Explain how air pollution and transportation affect each other.
Study the Clean Air Act and its results.

requirements.summary: Explore water pollution.

children.summary: Find where your water comes from and review a quality report.
Study the environmental effects of a local flood or drought.
Study the Clean Water Act and its results.

requirements.summary: Explore land pollution.

children.summary: List chemicals used on an area and their effects.
Study erosion at a real site and how to reduce it.
Study a Superfund site's cause, effects and cleanup.

requirements.summary: Explore rare, threatened or endangered species.

children.summary: Report on an endangered species in your state.
Report on a species that has recovered.
Visit a habitat project for a threatened or endangered species.

requirements.summary: Explore pollution prevention and conservation.

children.summary: Find five ways to save resources and practice two for a week.
Collect 10 examples of reduce, reuse, recycle, and explain them.
List five future household hazardous wastes and how to dispose of them.

requirements.summary: Explore pollination.

children.summary: List five local pollinators and the plants that draw them.
Watch flowers for an hour and record their pollinators.
Learn how pollinators support farming, with four crop examples.

requirements.summary: Investigate two invasive species in your area.
Identify a construction project's environmental impacts and alternatives.
Explore careers in environmental science and study one closely.

badges.name: Family Life
badges.summary: Explore what makes a family strong and do your part at home.

requirements.summary: Outline what a family is and why families matter.
Discuss why you're important to your family.
Do at least five chores for 90 days and keep a record.
Plan and complete a home project that helps your family.
Do a project with your family and discuss it.

children.summary: Its goal.
How each family member took part.
How it turned out.

requirements.summary: Plan and hold family meetings.

children.summary: Discuss how to plan and run a family meeting.
Make an agenda and hold meetings on these topics.
How the Scout Oath and Law shape your family life.
The biggest dangers and addictions young people face.
How growing up physically and mentally affects your choices.
Personal and family finances.
Handling a family crisis, and who can help.
How technology affects your family.
Good manners and etiquette.

requirements.summary: Discuss what makes a good parent or guardian.

badges.name: First Aid
badges.summary: Learn to prevent, recognize and treat injuries and sudden illnesses.

requirements.summary: Know how to handle a first aid emergency.

children.summary: Explain how to check the scene and assess the emergency.
Explain how to get help at home and in the backcountry.
Show how to prevent spreading infection and dispose of supplies.
Show how to check and manage airway and breathing.
Show a full exam of an injured person.
Explain why shock is an emergency.
Define triage and give examples.

requirements.summary: Get ready for first aid emergencies.

children.summary: Discuss the Scout health and medical record and why it matters.
Work with first-aid kits.
Build a hiking first-aid kit and show how to use it.
Inspect a unit, home, vehicle or camp kit with your counselor.

requirements.summary: Treat and prevent wounds that don't bleed outside.

children.summary: Bruises and hematomas.
Heat burns and scalds.
Chemical burns.
Electrical burns.
Sunburn.
Snow blindness.
Immersion foot, frostnip, frostbite and ice burns.
Scrapes such as chafing and rope burns.
Blisters.
Punctures from splinters, nails and fishhooks.
Poisonous plant rashes.
Chigger, tick, mosquito and gnat bites.
Bee stings.
Spider bites.
Scorpion stings.
Bites from pets, wild mammals or people.
Venomous snakebites.

requirements.summary: Treat and prevent bleeding wounds.

children.summary: Nosebleeds.
Scrapes and shallow cuts with mild bleeding.
Deep wounds with severe bleeding.
Explain when to use a tourniquet, and show applying one.

requirements.summary: Treat and prevent breathing emergencies.

children.summary: Choking.
Asthma attacks.
Anaphylaxis from stings, foods or other allergens.
Inhalation injuries.
Altitude sickness.

requirements.summary: Treat and prevent causes of losing consciousness.

children.summary: Fainting.
Low blood sugar.
Seizures.
Drug overdose and alcohol poisoning.
Blacking out underwater.
Cold water shock and drowning.
Lightning strikes and electric shock.

requirements.summary: Know how to respond to a heart attack.

children.summary: Explain what a heart attack is.
Describe its signs and first aid.
Explain when CPR should be given.
Show CPR on an approved training device.
Explain what an AED does.
Show or simulate using an AED.
Find AEDs in public places near you.

requirements.summary: Treat muscle and bone injuries.

children.summary: Compare strains, tears, ruptures, sprains, dislocations and fractures.
Describe signs of and first aid for strains, tears and ruptures.
Describe signs and complications of sprains, fractures and dislocations.
Show bandages for these injuries.
Slings for arm or collarbone fractures.
Wraps for a sprained ankle.
Wraps for a sprained wrist or hurt hand.
Show how to handle and splint fractures or dislocations.
Fingers and toes.
Forearm or wrist.
Upper leg.
Lower leg or ankle.

requirements.summary: Treat head and spine injuries.

children.summary: Describe head, neck and back injuries and how to prevent them.
Describe concussion signs and first aid.
Show how to bandage an open head wound.
Show first aid for a possible neck or back injury.

requirements.summary: Know when and how to move a patient.

children.summary: Explain when an injured person should or shouldn't be moved.
Choose and show ways to move someone.
Show solo and two-person carries out of a smoky room.
Do solo and partner carries for a sprained ankle, 25 yards.
Lead helpers to improvise a stretcher and carry someone 25 yards.

requirements.summary: Treat and prevent heat and cold conditions.

children.summary: Dehydration and overhydration.
Heat cramps and sore muscles after exercise.
Heat exhaustion.
Heatstroke.
Chest pain from cold exposure.
Hypothermia.

requirements.summary: Understand mental health conditions.

children.summary: Reactions to at least three stressful situations.
How to prepare for and handle those situations.
Signs someone may be a danger to themselves or others.
What to do if you think someone may be a danger.

requirements.summary: Treat and prevent other conditions.

children.summary: Something in the eye.
Damaged or knocked-out teeth.
Vomiting and diarrhea from food poisoning.
Stomach pain.
Stroke.

requirements.summary: Plan and teach a first aid skill using the EDGE method.
Explore emergency medical services.

children.summary: Visit an emergency medical station and learn about responders' work.
Interview an emergency medical professional about their career.
Explore careers in emergency medical services and study one.
Explore how emergency medical skills could become a hobby.

badges.name: Personal Fitness
badges.summary: Build healthy habits and follow a 12-week fitness program.

requirements.summary: Talk with your counselor about what being fit means to you.

children.summary: Describe a person in good physical shape.
Describe a person who is mentally, emotionally and socially healthy.
Describe a person who is spiritually healthy.
Explain why fitness in every area matters.
Connect each area of fitness to the Scout Oath and Law.

requirements.summary: Explain how you look after your health with regular checkups.

children.summary: Why yearly physicals matter and when you last had one.
Why dental care matters and when you last saw a dentist.

requirements.summary: Review your current health habits with your counselor.

children.summary: Your exercise habits and your long-term heart health risk.
Harmful substances you avoid and how that lowers your risk.
Diseases vaccines prevent and whether yours are up to date.
How food affects fitness and whether you eat a balanced diet.
What a healthy weight is for you and how you keep it.
Why sleep matters and whether you get enough.
Time with family and friends, and how you help at home.

requirements.summary: Pick, with your counselor, the fitness tests you'll repeat.

children.summary: A cardio test, usually a timed mile.
Two strength tests, one for core and one for upper body.
At least one flexibility test.

requirements.summary: Set your starting point before the program.

children.summary: Take your chosen tests and record the results.
Find your strongest and weakest areas; choose one to improve.
Keep a three-day log of what you eat and drink.
Use the log to set at least two eating goals.

requirements.summary: Plan a 12-week exercise and eating program.

children.summary: Include a warm-up.
Include cardio at least three times a week.
Include strength training.
Include flexibility exercises.
Include a cool-down.
Include how you'll reach your eating goals.

requirements.summary: Carry out your program and review the results.

children.summary: Follow your plan for 12 weeks and log each session.
Retake your tests at weeks 4 and 8 and after week 12.
Log your eating again at weeks 8 and 12 and check your goals.
Discuss your results and what you learned with your counselor.

requirements.summary: Look ahead at fitness in your future.

children.summary: Explore careers in fitness and study one closely.
Explore how fitness could become a lifelong hobby.

badges.name: Personal Management
badges.summary: Learn to budget, save, invest and manage your time.

requirements.summary: Plan how your family would buy something expensive.

children.summary: Pick a major purchase your family might make.
Write a plan to save for it.
Discuss it with your counselor.
Discuss it with your family.
Discuss how other family needs fit in.
Write a shopping strategy for it.
Judge its quality using ratings or reviews.
Compare prices from at least two sources.

requirements.summary: Budget and track your money for 13 weeks.

children.summary: Make a 13-week budget of income, expenses and savings.
Compare your expected income and expenses.
If you'd overspend, find ways to balance the budget.
If you'd have money left over, decide how to use it.
Record your actual income, expenses and savings for those weeks.
Compare your budget with what happened, and discuss changes.

requirements.summary: Discuss five ideas about money and how you feel about it.

children.summary: How getting money makes you feel.
How the cash you carry affects your spending.
Buyer's remorse, and how new things feel months later.
How hunger affects food shopping.
Whether something you bought lived up to its ads.
What happens to money in a savings account.
Charitable giving and why people give.
How you can manage your money better.

requirements.summary: Explain saving and investing basics.

children.summary: Saving versus investing, and when to use each.
Return on investment and risk.
Simple and compound interest.
Diversification.
Why saving for retirement matters.

requirements.summary: Explain how common investments work.

children.summary: Common stocks.
Mutual funds.
Life insurance.
Certificates of deposit.
Savings accounts.
U.S. savings bonds.

requirements.summary: Explain why people buy insurance and how it works.

children.summary: Car insurance.
Health insurance.
Homeowner's or renter's insurance.
Whole and term life insurance.

requirements.summary: Explain borrowing and credit.

children.summary: Loans, interest and APR.
Different ways to borrow.
Charge, debit and credit cards, and their costs and pitfalls.
Credit reports and how your choices affect them.
Ways to reduce or pay off debt.

requirements.summary: Practice managing your time for a week.

children.summary: List next week's tasks in order of importance.
Schedule a week of activities and tasks.
Follow your schedule and keep a daily diary.

columns.label: Tasks done, and when compared with your plan

children.summary: Review how your schedule worked and what you'd change.

requirements.summary: Write a plan for a project on paper.

children.summary: Define the goal.
Make a timeline of the steps.
Describe the project.
List the resources and how they'll help.
Make a budget.

requirements.summary: Look at a future career and its costs.

children.summary: Pick a career and discuss what it takes.
Explain its costs and how you'd pay for them.

badges.name: Swimming
badges.summary: Build swimming strokes, water safety and rescue skills.

requirements.summary: Know how to stay safe and healthy in the water.

children.summary: Review how Safe Swim Defense prevents common drownings.
Discuss preventing and treating swimming-related health problems.

requirements.summary: Pass the Scouting America swimmer test first.
Swim five strokes with good form.

children.summary: Front crawl or trudgen.
Back crawl.
Sidestroke.
Breaststroke.
Elementary backstroke.

requirements.summary: Swim 150 yards without stopping, using all five strokes.
Show water rescue skills.

children.summary: Show reaching and throwing rescues, and why they come first.
Show a line rescue as both tender and rescuer.

requirements.summary: Float and stay safe in the water.

children.summary: Float faceup for at least three minutes.
Survival float for at least five minutes.
Show the HELP and huddle positions in a life jacket.
Explain why swimming in cold water speeds hypothermia.

requirements.summary: Do surface dives in deep water.

children.summary: Surface dive feetfirst and bring up an object.
Surface dive headfirst and bring it up again.
Dive headfirst to 5 feet and swim underwater, three times.

requirements.summary: Show a standing headfirst dive and a long shallow dive.
Explain how swimming benefits fitness and health.
